The strongest man at the table chose to lose, and thatâs exactly why heâs the strongest. ðªâ¤ï¸

He didnât need the win. Everyone already knew what he could do. But that little girl didnât need to see a bodybuilder win. She needed to see her dad as a hero.

Thatâs what real strength looks like. Itâs not about proving yourself every chance you get. Itâs knowing which moments matter more than winning.

The people who are most secure in themselves are usually the ones who feel the least need to prove it. They donât chase every win or every bit of attention, because their confidence doesnât depend on it.

Thatâs what humility really is. Not thinking less of yourself, but being so sure of who you are that you can let someone else shine.

Insecure people need to win every battle. Humble people know when to let someone else have the moment.

Win where it counts. Let go where it doesnât.

During the Korean War in 1950, Turkish soldier SÃ¼leyman DilbirliÄi discovered a five-year-old Korean girl, Kim Eun-ja, who had been orphaned by the conflict. He took her into his care named her Ayla, and looked after her as his own daughter for more than a year. When he was ordered to return to Turkey, they were forced to separate, and Ayla was placed in an orphanage.

For decades, they lost contact until they were finally reunited in South Korea in 2010, nearly 60 years after their separation. In December 2017, Ayla returned to Turkey to see him one last time, shortly before he passed away aged 91.

On a summer evening in Boston, something remarkable happened in the American story. When Barack Obama walked onto the stage at the Democratic National Convention, he was not yet president or a household name, but there was a feeling that history was beginning to pay attention. His words carried more than ambition; they carried hope and faith in a country capable of overcoming its divisions and living up to the promises of its founding. In that moment, regardless of where people came from or which side they supported, they could feel the spirit of America growing stronger.
He spoke about unity in a way that felt genuine, not forced or simply designed to win applause, but inspired by something much deeper. He reminded Americans that the country was not divided into separate red and blue states, but united as one nation through shared dreams, challenges, and aspirations. For many people watching that night, his message was a powerful reminder of what America could be at its best: a place where opportunity is not limited to a privileged few, but available to anyone willing to work hard, dream big, and believe in a better future. It was the kind of speech that made people stand a little taller and feel proud of the nation they called home.
Looking back, that speech was more than just a moment in a political campaign; it was the beginning of something significant. It reminded people that leadership is not simply about holding power, but about serving a greater purpose. It showed that patriotism does not have to be loud or boastful, but can be expressed through quiet determination, lasting hope, and the belief that tomorrow can be better than today. On July 27, 2004, in Boston, Barack Obama reminded the nation that Americaâs story was far from finished, and that every generation has the opportunity to continue writing it with courage, conviction, and faith in the country they call home.

Pixarâs Inside Out (2015) features an emotional scene in which Joy and Bing Bong, Rileyâs long-forgotten imaginary friend, ride the Wagon of Wonders through the Memory Dump. Bing Bong, a whimsical creature made of cotton candy with cat, elephant, and dolphin features, helps Joy navigate Rileyâs mind while hoping to remain part of her memories.

The moment becomes heartbreaking when Bing Bong sacrifices himself so Joy can escape, gradually fading away as he asks her to take Riley to the moon for him. His disappearance represents the painful process of outgrowing childhood memories and imaginary companions. What begins as a playful adventure becomes one of the filmâs most emotional moments, reminding viewers that even the happiest memories can come with the sadness of letting go.

The 75-year-old Brooklyn sign painter has spent more than six decades painting old school hand-painted signs across New York. If youâve spent time in Bay Ridge, Coney Island or other parts of South Brooklyn, youâve probably seen his work without even realizing it. He retired about 10 years ago, but Tommy Holiday convinced him to pick up the brush again.

These days, a lot more signs are designed on computers and made by machines. Hand-painted signs arenât nearly as common as they once were, but thereâs something about them that you just canât replicate. Every brushstroke has a little personality to it. They feel alive. Mama came in because her appetite wasnât quite right and her exam told an important story. ð°

Sheâs carrying extra weight and has overgrown teeth, two problems that very often travel together in rabbits. The most common cause? Too many pellets and not enough roughage.

Rabbits are designed to chew fiber-rich hay almost constantly. That grinding motion is what naturally keeps their teeth worn down and their GI tract moving the way it should.

When pellets start to dominate the diet, we often see:
â¢ Weight gain
â¢ Dental overgrowth
â¢ Decreased appetite
â¢ GI slowdown

ð¡ Rule of thumb: most adult rabbits should get no more than Â¼ cup of pellets per day (and many need less depending on size and body condition).

The foundation of a healthy bunny diet should be:
ð¥¬ Unlimited grass hay (timothy, orchard, etc.)
ð¥¬ Daily leafy greens
ð¥ Pellets in measured amounts, not free-fed

If your rabbit is eating fewer hay strands and more pelletsâ¦ it may be time for a diet reset.

These are the humble heroes who embody the defining spirit of our nation.

They are the ones who embody that defining ethos and that constant call: to love your neighbor.

We need more people who live with that spirit. Who refuse to surrender to cynicism. Who have an indomitable will to serve, an invincible determination to bring hope in the face of despair, and the courage to act when others are in need.

May we see more of this.

Since some other platforms are starting to share our videos again from the seal jumping on the boat we were on, I thought I would make a shorter version of the experience and share it again. Itâs almost been a full year since it happened! If you want to watch the full thing, the videos are pinned on my page. A few things to answer/mention that have come up in the comments;
1. Why didnât we leave once the seal was on the boat? We legally couldnât turn then engines on with the orcas that close to us, we also wouldnât want to! We love the orcas that visit our waters and wouldnât want to cause any situation that would possibly hurt them, especially turning on an engine that could cut them. 
2. Werenât you afraid they were going to tip the boat? Absolutely not! Not all orcas are the same and Biggs orcas have never been documented trying to tip, flip or mess with boats. There is an Iberian ecotype of orca that have made headlines for dismantling sailboat rudders, but these are not the same ecotype of orca. 
3. âThe orcas are starving, let them eat the seal!â We have two ecotypes of orcas that visit the Puget sound; the southern residents and Biggs orcas. The southern resident orcas are indeed starving and need our help, however, they eat salmon, not seals. The orcas in our video are Biggs orcas and they have absolutely no problem finding food. They also had ample time to consume this seal as they used it as hunting practice for the younger orcas in the group for an entire 30 minutes before it spotted us on the boat. It also fell off the boat and could have been caught then as well. 
4. âI would have pushed that seal back inâ another illegal act if we were to do that. Seals are protected under the marine mammal protection act so you cannot touch them. Also, we arenât assholes!
5. âI hope the seal was able to find its way homeâ seals live a nomadic lifestyle and do not typically stay in one area long term. We were also not in open ocean, we were in a channel in the Puget sound and drove the seal maybe 2 miles or so (probably less) closer to the shore line. @fuzzysmith22 #orca #killerwhale #naturephotography #orcawhale #pacificnorthwest

A birthday cake. A family that sings to you. A home where people actually remember the day you were born. For most of us, those are so normal that we barely think twice about them. Some years we donât even feel like celebrating.

But for a lot of people in this world, those simple moments never came. No candles, no gifts, no one making a big deal about them. Not because they didnât deserve it, but because nobody was there to give it to them.

Thatâs what makes gratitude so powerful. It reminds you that the âordinaryâ parts of your life are someone elseâs dream. The meal on your table. The people who call to check on you. The family that shows up for you, flaws and all.

And it goes both ways. You never know how much a small act of love can mean to someone whoâs never had it. Something that costs you very little could be the moment they remember for the rest of their life.

Appreciate what you have, and never underestimate what you can give.

One of the most philosophical moments in animation history comes from a krill in âHappy Feet Two.â

Brad Pitt and Matt Damon voice Will and Bill, two tiny krill whose 3-minute comedic subplot gradually turns into a surprisingly thoughtful debate about the meaning of life.

While Bill finds comfort in the familiar, Will begins questioning why he and millions of other krill spend their entire lives blindly following the swarm, never stopping to ask where theyâre going or whether thereâs something more to life than simply doing what everyone else does.

Beneath all the absurd humor and frankly exceptional krill puns lies an unexpectedly profound reflection on the search for oneâs place and purpose in the world. A deeply human debate about the existence of free will, told through the eyes of one of the oceanâs tiniest creatures.

A bride in Jiangsu province turned her wedding into a hardware unboxing ceremony when she surprised her gamer groom with an ASUS ROG Astral RTX 5090 â one of the most powerful (and hardest to get) consumer graphics cards on the planet.

She didn't just hand it over. First, she made him solve a math puzzle built from Chinese internet love codes: 520 Ã 10 + 1314 â 514 â 619 + 666 â 957. In Chinese online slang, 520 sounds like "I love you" and 1314 sounds like "forever." The answer: 5090, the exact model number of the GPU waiting backstage. Only after he cracked it did staff bring out the box.

The groom tore it open, recognized the card, and immediately broke down crying â then held it over his head like a championship trophy and paraded it past the guests. The emcee roasted him gently, telling him to "take the fruit of your life and show it off."

Here's the kicker: this specific RTX 5090 variant isn't even officially sold in mainland China through normal retail channels, making it a genuine white-whale item for Chinese PC builders. Overseas it retails around $2,799, but scarcity has pushed street prices far higher. For a groom described as a hardcore gaming and hardware enthusiast, the gift was basically a love letter written in silicon and VRAM.

#ChinaInsiderNews #PCGaming #ChineseWedding #LoveStory

Never forget how many people are struggling.(20)

Over the years, I have spoken face-to-face with thousands of residents across Mississauga.

I have heard many stories.

While visiting residents, I met a man from Ward 8.

He had immigrated to Canada 21 years ago.

He told me that since coming to Canada, he had never gone to a barber shop.

It wasnât because he didnât care about his appearance.

It wasnât because he didnât want a nice haircut.

He simply couldnât afford it.

More than 20 years ago, when he first arrived in Canada, he had about $5,000 to his name.

A friend helped him rent a place, which cost him $2,000.

He bought some basic food and household necessities, and a used bicycle.

Soon, he had only a little more than $2,000 left.

But the next monthâs rent was already waiting.

So he needed to find a job immediately.

He eventually found work washing dishes.

He told me that for the first three months, he didnât even get a haircut.

After all, he was working in a kitchen and didnât have to meet customers.

Then his wife found a used set of hair-cutting tools at a yard sale.

From that day on, his wife cut his hair.

At first, she wasnât very experienced, so he simply kept his head shaved.

About a year later, she became better at it, and he started growing his hair again.

I thought about that story for a long time.

And then I met other residents.

Some were from Ward 4. Some were from Ward 7.

Why?

Because there are so many bills.

Rent. Property taxes. Utilities. Food. Transportation.

Each bill may seem manageable by itself.

But together, they can become a heavy burden on an ordinary family.

And it made me think:

If a family had a little less financial pressure every month, would they have a little more choice?

Maybe they could get a haircut at a barber shop once in a while.

Maybe they could buy something new for their children.

This is how I think about local government.

Behind every number is a family.
Behind every tax decision is a personâs life.

When household incomes are limited and the cost of living keeps rising, every dollar matters.
Never forget those who are struggling.

Cats have been part of human life for at least 9,500 years. In Cyprus, archaeologists found one buried beside a person. Cats were not native to the island, meaning someone had brought it there by boat.

In ancient Egypt, cats were associated with Bastet, a goddess of protection. They appeared in bronze sculptures and were mummified as offerings. Later, they travelled across the Mediterranean and spread through Europe during the Roman period.

In China, the story began with a different cat altogether. Wild leopard cats lived near farming villages more than 5,000 years ago, hunting the rodents attracted to stored grain. The domestic cats we know today arrived there centuries later along the Silk Road. Across places and eras, cats moved from the edges of settlements into peopleâs homes, art and beliefs.

Most people are too busy thinking about their own lives to spend much time judging yours. ð§ â¤ï¸

Think about how many things youâve wanted to do but talked yourself out of because you were worried about what other people might think.

Starting a business. Changing careers. Pursuing an unusual dream. Putting yourself out there and risking embarrassment.

The truth is that most people are far more concerned with their own problems, insecurities, and ambitions than they are with your decisions.

The fear of being judged can control your life far more than the judgment itself ever will.

People might notice when you fail. They might even talk about it. But eventually, theyâll return to their own lives while youâre still living with the decisions you made.

And thatâs where the freedom comes from.

You get one life to live. Donât spend it trying to impress people who arenât the ones who have to live it.

label_values.value: Kailasa was just scanned with Lasers, and if you havenât been following this place hold on because whatâs been uncovered inside wont just rewrite Indian History, its going to rewrite human history and prove that the tools Ancient india possessed were even more advanced than our own. But you have to know what youâre looking at first. Kailasa is not built, it was removed from the side of a mountain, Meaning there could be no mistakes made when carving one of the hardest rocks on earth. The amount of Basalt removed to create the temple is between 200,000 and 400,000 tons. The first mystery is we dont know where it went. We also dont know when this thing was built. The main dating source are two land grants. If you look at a map of india, kailasa is here. The first land grant was found here, roughly 200 miles away, the second was here, roughly  400 miles away. Dating would be useful because we could know what tools they used to carve it. Ancient india had steel in 600BC that would later become the famous damascus steel. In 1682 a Mughal emperor ordered 1000 workers to destroy the temple. The damage to the sculptures is extensive and honestly, one of the most disrespectful things ever done in history. But theres a silver lining. It showed just how hard this basalt is. Even with modern much more durable alloys, humans barely make a dent. Basalt is hardened lava, a 6 on the Mohs scale meaning steel barely makes a scratch. So the russians carried out an experiment. What they did was have 3 different people take a whack at this stuff using modern tools. The volume removed was measured using photogrammetry Keep in mind the marks made look absolutely nothing like the marks we actually see on the wall. The results? Only 1 cubic meter of basalt could be removed if a person worked for 3 years straight every day.  Since Kailasa is unfinished, we actaully have the witness marks or tool marks that prove a different method was used. The depth of the cuts in Kailasa exceed what hydraulic breakers are capable of. Season 1 was originally supposed to be five episodes but grew to eight, later bringing in Minecraft YouTubers like DanTDM, CaptainSparklez, Stampy Cat and LDShadowLady as themselves. It was eventually turned into an interactive Netflix series, then became surprisingly hard to legally access after Telltale shut down and the series was removed from digital stores.

What happens when a child meets the people she was taught to fear? ð¯ðµ

Michiko Kornhauser was a child living in Okayama, Japan, during World War II. Like many Japanese children at the time, she grew up during intense wartime propaganda that portrayed Americans as enemies. But after Japan surrendered in August 1945, the situation changed dramatically. American forces entered Japan as part of the Allied occupation, and Michiko eventually had her first personal encounter with an American GI.

That moment was significant because it challenged something much more powerful than a simple wartime image of an enemy: a belief she had grown up with. Japan's surrender ended the war, but the occupation that followed brought Japanese civilians into everyday contact with American soldiers. For children like Michiko, meeting an American in person could be a striking contrast to the frightening picture of Americans they had been taught during the war.

Her memory gives a personal view of a much larger historical transitionâfrom wartime hatred and fear to an occupation in which former enemies suddenly had to live alongside one another. Stories like this show how quickly the meaning of an "enemy" could change once the fighting was over. ð

There was something special about Fortnite Chapter 1 Season 7.

The snow had arrived, planes were flying across the sky, and the whole island suddenly felt like a winter playground. Polar Peak towered over the frozen landscape, Happy Hamlet felt like a cozy little escape, and the mysterious iceberg had appeared off the coast.

But honestly, it was more than the map.

It was the feeling.

You could load into a match with no idea what was going to happen. Maybe you would land at Tilted Towers, spend five minutes building like your life depended on it, then somehow escape with barely any health. Maybe you would wander around the snowy areas with your friends, laughing at absolutely nothing.

And then there were the little moments. Finding a new location for the first time. Hearing the snow crunch beneath your characterâs feet. Discovering that giant iceberg and wondering what Epic Games had planned next. Waiting for the next update and immediately jumping into the game to see what had changed.

Season 7 felt like a time when Fortnite was not just a game you played. It was a place you visited.

Looking back, that might be what makes it so nostalgic. It was the music, the loading screens, the old map, the winter atmosphere, and most importantly, the people you played with.

You probably did not realize it at the time, but those ordinary Fortnite nights were becoming memories.

And that is why Chapter 1 Season 7 still feels so magical.

The Chicago White Sox completed one of the most incredible turnarounds in MLB history, clinching a postseason berth just two years after setting a modern MLB record with 121 losses. After three straight 100-loss seasons, the White Sox officially turned things around with a 9-1 win over the Kansas City Royals.

Chicago went 61-101 in 2023, 41-121 in 2024, and 60-102 in 2025. Then, in 2026, the White Sox finished 84-78 and secured a playoff spot, becoming the first team in baseball history to reach the postseason after three consecutive 100-loss seasons. It also marks their first winning season and playoff appearance since 2021.

A major part of the turnaround came from a roster overhaul, with the team adding young talent and key contributors such as Japanese star Munetaka Murakami, Miguel Vargas, and Braden Montgomery. Strong leadership and a major cultural shift under manager Will Venable also helped transform the team from a struggling franchise into a legitimate playoff contender.

frosted blueberry banana loaf ð« 

im super picky about banana bread and my husband loves when i make it, so i love spicing it up in different ways! this bread is loaded with blueberries and so yummy! hereâs how i made it :) 

ingredients:
3 very ripe bananas 
3/4 cup maple syrup 
1/3 cup oil (i like avocado oil) 
1 tsp vanilla 
1 egg
1 tsp baking soda 
1 tsp baking powder 
1/4 tsp salt 
1 1/2 cups AP flour 
2 cups wild blueberries 

make it:
in a bowl, mash bananas until you can mix well. next add wet ingredients: maple syrup, oil, eggs, and vanilla. once wet ingredients are mixed in, add baking soda, baking powder and salt. slowly add in flour, careful not to over mix. add in blueberries. pour into a bread pan and top with more blueberries if youâd like. 

bake at 350 for about an hour and 10 minutes to an hour and 30 minutes. baking time will vary depending on if you use fresh or frozen blueberries. i love frozen wild blueberries but the baking time is more like an hour and 30 because of the extra moisture, so just be aware! the bread is done when a toothpick comes out clean or mostly clean :) 

for the glaze, i added 2 cups of powdered sugar into a bowl along with a tsp of vanilla and a handful of mashed blueberries. mix while slowly adding a couple splashes of heavy cream until you get a super thick and creamy consistency. pour ontop of cooled bread and let set for about 10 minutes and serve! if youâd love blueberries like me i hope you love this :)

France and Belgium have often found themselves on the same side during major European conflicts. Since Belgium gained independence in 1830, the two countries have maintained close political, economic, and military ties, particularly during the World Wars.

In World War I, Belgium was invaded in 1914 after Germany advanced through its territory to reach France. Belgian resistance slowed the invasion, while French and British forces fought alongside Belgium on the Western Front. The defense of Belgium became a symbol of Allied cooperation during the war.

A similar situation occurred in World War II. Germany invaded both Belgium and France in May 1940, leading to intense fighting across Belgian territory. Although both countries were eventually occupied, Belgian and French soldiers continued to contribute to the Allied war effort through resistance movements and forces fighting abroad.

Following World War II, France and Belgium became founding members of NATO and key participants in European integration. Today, the two neighboring countries are close allies, sharing strong economic, political, and cultural connections.

Thai tea brown sugar tiramisu recipe!!

Your favorite boba tea flavor turned into a tiramisu, what more can you wish for?

For everyone asking about the Osta app, check the link in my bio or look up âOsta recipesâ in the App Store or Google play store!

Makes 1 deep baking dish 

Thai tea brown sugar mascarpone cream
- 3 egg yolks
- 50g dark brown sugar
- 30g granulated sugar
- 6g Thai tea leaves
-1/2tsp vanilla 
- Pinch salt
- 230g (8oz) mascarpone 
- 300g heavy cream, chilled 

- A pack of ladyfingers (you wonât use all)

Thai tea soak
- 28g Thai tea leaves
- 1 1/2 cup hot water
- 2tsp dark brown sugar

Filling:
1. In a blender, blitz the dark brown sugar, granulated sugar and Thai tea until it becomes a fine powder.
2. Add the blitzed sugar + Thai tea mixture to the egg yolks and place over a double boiler. (The bottom of the bowl shouldnât touch the water). Whisk until doubled in size 
3. Add the vanilla and salt and set aside.
4. To another bowl, add the mascarpone and heavy cream. Whip until medium peaks form about 5 mins (do not over-whip otherwise it will become grainy)
5. Add the egg yolk mixture to the cream and gently fold until incorporated. 

Thai tea soak:
1. Steep the Thai tea with 1 1/2 cup
hot water and let it sit for 5 mins. Strain well.

Assembly:
1. Dip each ladyfinger into the thai tea soak and cover the bottom layer of the baking dish.
2. Add 1/2 of the cream mixture and evenly spread over using a spatula. 
3. Repeat steps 1-2 once more 
4. Chill for at least 5 hours, ideally overnight 
5. Before serving, dust with FINELY powdered Thai tea or coco powder and enjoy

ð¬Your Lie in April > is about a Japan where classical music competitions are everything for young prodigies. Kosei Arima was known as a human metronome â a child pianist who played exactly what his strict mother taught him, winning every contest. But after his mother died, he lost his ability to hear his own piano, and his monochrome world went silent.

The story starts when Kosei, now a dull 14-year-old in middle school avoiding the piano, meets Kaori Miyazono. She's a free-spirited violinist in the same school who plays wildly, colorfully, and completely by her own rules, and she needs a pianist to accompany her for a competition. She drags Kosei back to music, forces him to play again, and with her friends Tsubaki and Watari, turns his gray life back into something loud and messy. What Kosei doesn't know is that Kaori is hiding a secret of her own about why she chose him in the first place.

At its core, it's a music anime with the soul of a coming-of-age romance. Half the time it's breathtaking performances animated by A-1 Pictures where every note feels like it's shaking on screen, and the other half it's just kids walking home from school, arguing in the music room, eating pork buns, and trying to figure out how to say what they feel before it's too late. It's bright, heartbreaking, and beautiful all at once â and that's why people never forget it.

In the Japanese dub of SpongeBob SquarePants, Plankton undergoes a fascinating character transformation driven by voice acting choices that sound radically different from the western original. While Mr. Lawrence originally gave Plankton a booming, deep, and theatrical villain voice, Japanese voice actor ChÃµ reimagined the tiny copepod with an insanely high-pitched, manic, and shrill delivery.

Rather than sounding like a sinister mastermind with a deep baritone, the Japanese dub emphasizes Planktonâs microscopic size through frantic, squeaky rants. His unhinged, high-frequency tantrums make his huge megalomaniacal schemes feel even more absurd and tragic. This stark vocal shift turns Plankton into a hilariously chaotic, eccentric underdog, proving how a radically different voice performance can give an iconic animated character a fresh comedic identity.

The Office (2005â2013) is a comedy about an ordinary workplace that slowly becomes a story about friendship, growing up, finding your people, and the strange little moments that make life memorable. And among all its relationships, Michael and Holly have something especially beautiful about them. They just get each other â the same weird sense of humour, the same awkwardness, the same willingness to be completely themselves. What starts as a friendship turns into a love story that survives distance, bad timing, and separation before bringing them back together.
Holly doesn't just fall in love with Michael; she understands the person underneath all the jokes and chaos. And Michael, after spending so much of his life searching for love, finally finds someone with whom he doesn't have to pretend to be someone else. Their relationship feels less like a perfect romance and more like two wonderfully strange people finally finding the person who speaks their language.
And maybe that's what makes The Office so special. We came for the comedy, but somewhere along the way, these people became our people too.

PING PONG THE ANIMATION

Ping Pong the Animation is a coming-of-age sports anime directed by Masaaki Yuasa and based on the manga by Taiyo Matsumoto.

The story follows two childhood friends and table tennis prodigies:

* Makoto âSmileâ Tsukimoto â a quiet, emotionally reserved player with exceptional talent.
* Yutaka âPecoâ Hoshino â an outgoing, confident player who dreams of becoming the worldâs best.

As they compete against increasingly skilled rivals, including the disciplined Chinese player Wenge âChinaâ Kong and the intimidating ace RyÅ«ichi âDragonâ Kazama, the series explores much more than sports. It examines ambition, talent, pressure, identity, friendship, and what it means to pursue excellence.

Rather than focusing solely on winning tournaments, the anime delves into the psychological struggles of its characters. Each player confronts personal insecurities and asks whether they play for victory, recognition, joy, or something deeper.

What makes it stand out

* Highly distinctive, unconventional art style.
* Deep character development for nearly every major player.
* Strong themes of self-discovery and personal growth.
* A focus on the mental and emotional side of competition rather than just match results.

In 1969, the number one song in America was by a band that actually didnât exist. That song was Sugar, Sugar by The Archies.

The Archies came from the animated TV show The Archie Show, which was based on the Archie Comics characters. The song was recorded by studio musicians rather than an actual touring band, and its catchy bubblegum pop sound helped it become a massive hit. It spent four weeks at number one on the Billboard Hot 100 and became one of the biggest singles of the entire year.

The success of Sugar, Sugar proved that music tied to fictional characters could dominate real-world charts, making it one of the most unusual number one hits in American music history.

A curious bear cub took a little nibble of a photographerâs boot while he was on a tour in Alaska on August 2.

Video taken by nature and wildlife photographer Bruce Robert Danz shows three and an adult grizzly walking out of the water, passing close by Danz and another photographer.

In the footage, the photographers can be heard saying, âNo bear, no bear,â to encourage the bears to keep walking. However, one cub couldnât help itself and stopped to nibble on Danzâs shoe.

âJust moving my boot a little was enough to end the interaction and the cub fell back in line,â Danz told Storyful.

The interaction happened while Danz was on a photographic tour with Jerry Jacques of Alaska Grizzly Safaris, Danz said.

âWe kept our distance, kept quiet and did not disturb the bears from fishing,â Danz said. âThe bears were aware of our presence and occasionally would walk very close to us.â

âJerry said we handled the situation perfectly by not causing alarm,â Danz said. âJerry suggested perhaps the cub was tired of salmon and wanted to try some filet of sole. I was not afraid, just intent on keeping quiet and not causing alarm.â

Belgium repeatedly found itself trapped between France and Germany because of its location. Sitting directly between the two powers, Belgium became strategically important whenever war broke out in Western Europe. France often viewed Belgian territory as a defensive buffer that could keep German armies farther away from Paris, while Germany saw Belgium as the fastest route around Franceâs heavily defended eastern frontier.

This became especially important during both World Wars. Germany invaded Belgium in 1914 to attack France from the north, and did so again in 1940. France responded by moving troops into Belgium because it expected the main German attack to come through the country. In that sense, Belgium often became the battlefield where France and Germany tried to gain an advantage over one another, even though Belgium itself usually wanted to remain neutral and stay out of their wars.

ð : Big World ( 2024 )

Big World is not just a film about disability. It is a film about wanting to be seen as a whole person.

Directed by Yang Lina and led by Jackson Yee as Liu Chunhe, the film follows a young man with cerebral palsy as he tries to find his place in a world that constantly underestimates him. While helping his grandmother pursue her long-held dream, Chunhe slowly begins to understand his own dreams, desires, and the kind of life he wants for himself.

What makes Big World so moving is that it refuses to reduce Chunhe to his disability. He is a grandson, a friend, a son, a young man capable of falling in love, making mistakes, dreaming of a future, and wanting independence. His biggest struggle is not simply with his body, but with a society that has already decided what his life should look like.

The film also beautifully explores the complicated love within families. Sometimes love can become protection. Protection can become control. And the people who love us the most can unintentionally become the people who make it hardest for us to become independent.

At its core, Big World asks a simple but powerful question: Who gets to decide what a meaningful life looks like?

It is tender without being sentimental, emotional without constantly asking for sympathy, and deeply rooted in the ordinary moments that make a life feel real.

And perhaps that is the meaning behind its title. The world may build barriers around you, but your dreams do not have to become smaller because of them.

Sometimes, all a person needs is the chance to discover just how big their world can actually be. ð¬

The painting was completed in 1743 by Korean court artist Kim Doo-ryang and the poem was written by King Yeongjo.

Yeongjo ruled Joseon from 1724 to 1776, during a period when the royal court was deeply divided by competing political factions. 

He promoted a policy known as Tangpyeong, or âimpartiality,â intended to reduce factional conflict and prevent any single group from dominating government.

The poem has been interpreted as Yeongjo rebuking officials who were neglecting their responsibilities while spending their energy fighting political rivals. 

In other words, nearly 300 years ago, a Korean king used a dog poem to tell his government officials: stop barking at each other and do your jobs!

Arcane (2021 - 2024) | Christian Linke & Alex Yee

 Arcane (2021) is a breathtaking triumph of world-building that elevates video game adaptations from visual novelties into genuine narrative art. Produced by Fortiche Production, the series abandons standard animation tropes in favor of a hybrid aesthetic, blending hand-painted digital texturing with expressive 3D character rigging. Every single frame feels like a living oil painting, heavy with ambient light and textural richness that mirrors the stark thematic contrast between the sleek, utopian heights of Piltover and the bio-luminescent, neon-drenched squalor of Zaun.

Beyond its technical perfection, the show operates on a level of cinematic literacy rare for serialized animation. The editing relies on rhythmic cross-cutting, thematic match cuts, and aggressive montage to mirror the fractured mental state of its central anti-hero, Jinx. The tragic rift between sisters Jinx and Vi isn't driven by simple villainy, but by structural oppression, psychological trauma, and opposing philosophies of survival. Driven by meticulous framing, kinetic camera movements, and an impeccably curated soundtrack, the series achieves an impressive balance of visceral action and deep emotional weight.

How Rooftop Koreans dealt with the worst riots in American history.
â£
In spring 1992, Los Angeles was burning. The police had pulled out of Koreatown and 911 had stopped answering. On the rooftops of their own shops, Korean store owners lay behind rifles and shotguns, watching the fires crawl closer. The crowds below expected easy pickings, but they had no idea who they were dealing with.
â£
The riots had started days earlier, when a jury cleared four Los Angeles policemen who had been filmed beating a man named Rodney King. The city exploded, and while the police fell back to protect the wealthier districts, Koreatown, a neighborhood of Korean immigrant families and their small shops, was left to burn. One patrol car did stop at a grocery store where armed guards stood watch: the officer told them to raise their hands, realized they were only protecting their own shop, and drove off. He was the last policeman the owner saw for the rest of the riots.
â£
But many of the shop owners had served in the South Korean military, and they hadnât forgotten how to fight. With the power out, a local station called Radio Korea became their lifeline: it broadcast which blocks were under attack, called for armed volunteers, and sent groups of Korean Marine veterans wherever things looked worst.
â£
At one large grocery store, twenty armed men barricaded the parking lot behind trucks and luxury cars. One of them had brought an old machine gun. When the looters advanced at nightfall, the defenders fired into the air, then put a few rounds in the ground in front of the crowd. The looters turned around and never came back. The owner ate and slept in that parking lot for three days. Not a single person was hurt.
â£
Koreatown still paid a brutal price: more than 2,000 Korean-owned businesses were destroyed, nearly half the damage of the entire riots. But where the owners stood together, the stores held. One shopkeeper had fired five hundred rounds into the air to save a single mall, and when a reporter found him afterwards, he stated: âWe have lost our faith in the police. Where were you when we needed you?â

The only way to stop violent bad people, is violent good people.

The wildest part? It was made entirely by two people: the director and his mother, who is in her 60s. With no professional team and almost no budget, she learned animation as they went and even sang the ending song.
After five years of work, the film unexpectedly went viral across Chinese social media. Within just a few days, its box office surpassed 9 million yuan, placing it among the Top 10 domestic animated films of the year.
For many viewers, it became more than just a movieâit turned into an internet phenomenon, with audiences laughing, sharing memes and joining the conversation online.

A 5,700-pound electric SUV just drove completely upside down across the ceiling of a tunnel. ð¤¯ ðï¸ 

Voyahâs Passion S completed a full 360-degree loop inside a closed test tunnel in Wuhan, China, recreating a stunt made famous by Mercedes-Benz 16 years earlier.

Mercedes showcased the concept with the SLS AMG in 2010. Now, Voyah says its electric SUV completed the maneuver at roughly 130 km/h (81 mph), using an all-wheel-drive powertrain producing approximately 637 horsepower and 765 Nm of torque.

The physics are just as remarkable as the footage. At sufficient speed, the curvature of the tunnel and the vehicleâs momentum create the centripetal acceleration necessary to keep the SUV pressed against the surface, even while completely upside down.

More than a decade after the idea captured the worldâs attention, a nearly three-ton electric SUV just put its own version on the ceiling.

Conversely, some observers argue that the interactions are within the spirit of the parkâs guest-character experiences and that the fan is simply a dedicated visitor.The controversy has also brought attention back to the âPeter Pandomâ subculture that was once prominent on platforms like Tumblr, which involved intense focus on specific park performers. Marcus Smart wasnât drafted to be the star. When he entered the NBA, most of the attention was on scorers and highlight players. Smart built his reputation differently â through defense, hustle, and doing the work most players avoid.

Early in his career with the Boston Celtics, he took on the toughest assignments every night. Diving for loose balls, guarding bigger players, making plays that donât always show up in stats â he became known for effort before recognition.

Years later, that identity paid off. He became the first guard in decades to win NBA Defensive Player of the Year, proving that impact isnât always about scoring â itâs about consistency and commitment to the role.

People notice the awards now.
They donât see the possessions where he chose effort over comfort.

Not every path to success is flashy.
Sometimes doing the hard things every day is what separates you.

December NFL snow games are some of the most iconic moments in football, where freezing temperatures, heavy snowfall, and strong winds create unforgettable matchups. Teams like the Buffalo Bills, Green Bay Packers, Chicago Bears, and Cleveland Browns are known for playing in harsh winter conditions that can completely change the way games are played. Passing becomes difficult, kicking is unpredictable, and games often turn into physical, run-heavy battles.

Some of the most famous snow games include the 2017 âSnow Bowlâ between the Bills and Colts, where players were running through nearly a foot of snow and Buffalo won in overtime. The 1982 AFC Championship, nicknamed the âFreezer Bowl,â saw the Bengals defeat the Chargers in wind chills approaching -60Â°F. More recently, the 2022 Bills vs. Dolphins game featured heavy snowfall in the second half, creating one of the seasonâs most memorable finishes.

For NFL fans, December snow games represent the toughest and most exciting part of the season. The weather adds an unpredictable element that tests playersâ toughness, coaching decisions, and ball security, often leading to unforgettable highlights. Whether itâs quarterbacks throwing through blizzards or running backs carving paths through deep snow, these games have become a defining tradition of late-season football. #jameiswinston #christmas #football #nfl #viral

Kroshik is a famous Ladoga ringed seal whose unusual rescue story began in March 2016, when fishermen found him alone on the shore of Lake Ladoga in Russia. The tiny pup was severely underweight, dehydrated and exhausted, weighing just 4 kilograms when rescuers from the Baltic Seal Friends Foundation took him in. ð¦­ 

After months of rehabilitation, rescuers tried to return Kroshik to the wild, but he had other plans. He became unusually attached to humans and, after being released, returned to his rescuers. A second attempt to return him to the wild also failed, leading specialists to keep him permanently at their marine mammal rehabilitation center near St. Petersburg. Kroshik has since become one of the centerâs most famous residents and an ambassador for the conservation of Ladoga ringed seals.

Fun Fact: In *Jujutsu Kaisen*, Aoi Todo's insane bromance with his "besto friendo" Yuji Itadori and his legendary, over-the-top crush on Takada-chan are the perfect mix of peak comedy, loyalty, and unhinged energy that make him one of the most memorable side characters ever! ð¤ðªâ¤ï¸

Todo's whole personality flips the switch the moment he asks Yuji the iconic question: "What kind of girls do you like?" When Yuji answers "tall girls with a big ass" (in the heat of battle, no less), Todo instantly declares him his brother from another motherâlike, full adoption papers signed in blood mid-fight! From that second on, Todo treats Yuji like family: hyping him up, fighting back-to-back, crying manly tears when Yuji "dies" in Shibuya, and straight-up refusing to believe he's gone because "my brother wouldn't die that easily!" It's the most wholesome, ride-or-die bond in the seriesâTodo would burn the world for Yuji without a second thought! ð¥ð

Then there's his undying love for Takada-chan, the idol from his favorite late-night show. This 6'3" battle maniac with a Boar-tusk headband turns into a blushing, heart-eyed simp the moment her name comes upâhe's got her posters, watches every episode religiously, screams her catchphrases in fights ("Takada-chan is the best!"), and even uses her as motivation to go harder ("For Takada-chan's smile!"). It's so pure and ridiculous that even Gojo teases him about itâTodo doesn't care, he's locked in for life! ðð

The combo is chef's kiss: unbreakable brotherly love for Yuji that hits you in the feels, and a celebrity crush so intense it powers his Black Flash and Boogie Woogie swaps. Todo isn't just strongâhe's emotionally all-in on the people (and idol) he cares about, making every scene with him explode with hype, laughs, and unexpected depth! ðð¤

This video captures from the outset a poignant contrast between former college football player Greg Brooks Jr.âs current life and his past athletic career. It begins with emotional interview clips, starting with an older press conference where Brooks discusses dealing with vertigo. The footage then shifts to an ABC News Exclusive interview where it is revealed that Brooks has not heard from the LSU coaching staff, specifically head coach Brian Kelly, since October 2023. A family member next to him emphasizes the hurt this caused, urging Kelly to simply call and show care. In a subsequent podcast appearance, Brooks is asked if he misses the game, admitting it is difficult to watch on screen knowing that should be him. The segment concludes on a somber note as Brooks is wheeled away and the host breaks down in tears.

The second half of the video transitions into a dynamic compilation of Brooks' highlights on the football field, celebrating his athletic legacy. The footage showcases his time playing as number 9 for the Arkansas Razorbacks and number 3 for the LSU Tigers. It features a sequence of his most impressive plays, including intense tackles, interceptions, and key defensive moments. The vibrant game-day clips provide a sharp contrast to the previous emotional interviews, serving as a powerful reminder of his impact on the field before his health struggles.

Will Smith recently sparked a wave of online jokes after sharing a story about growing up in Philadelphia, where he explained that he and his friends would spend time "busting on each other"âan old-school phrase meaning to roast or tease one another. As the clip spread across social media, many younger viewers misheard the expression as "bussin on each other," giving the story an entirely different meaning through modern internet slang.

The misunderstanding quickly turned the interview into a viral meme, with fans joking about the accidental double meaning. The mention of Flavor Flav only added to the comedy, making the clip even more entertaining. What started as a nostalgic story about friendly banter became a perfect example of how changing slang and generational differences can create hilarious viral moments.

Directed by Robert De Niro in his directorial debut, A Bronx Tale (1993) is a compelling, vibrant coming-of-age gangster drama that masterfully explores the tug-of-war between honest labor. Set against the backdrop of the 1960s Bronx, the film follows Calogero, a young Italian-American boy who finds himself torn between two powerful father figures: his hardworking, straight-arrow bus driver father, Lorenzo (played by De Niro), and Sonny (Chazz Palminteri), a charismatic local mafia boss who takes the boy under his wing. Adapted from Palminteri's autobiographical one-man play, the movie transcends the typical gangster genre by focusing heavily on themes of loyalty, racial tension, and the weight of personal choices, ultimately delivering a poignant, street-smart story about the tragedy of wasted talent.

He told Chazz it was the best one-man show heâd ever seen and made a gentlemen's agreement: De Niro would direct, play the bus-driver father, and protect Chazz's right to write the script and star as Sonny. When SpongeBob SquarePants first hit Nickelodeon in 1999, the early seasons werenât just a regular cartoonâthey were carefully built around a very specific idea: a genuinely soft-hearted character living in a loud, absurd world.

At the center of it all is SpongeBob himselfâendlessly optimistic, emotionally open, and almost childlike in his sincerity. What made those early episodes so special is that the writers, led by creator SpongeBob SquarePantsâs original vision under Stephen Hillenburg, intentionally leaned into that contrast. The jokes were sharp and surreal, but SpongeBobâs core never changed: he cares too much, feels too deeply, and genuinely believes the world is goodâeven when Bikini Bottom clearly isnât.

That balance is what defined Seasons 1â3. Behind the chaos of jellyfishing, Krabby Patties, and Squidwardâs misery was a character written with emotional honesty. The writers often pushed SpongeBob into ridiculous situations, but always brought him back to that same soft centerâkindness, loyalty, and an almost unshakable innocence.

A familiar song, place, photo, or even a random memory can suddenly bring an old friend to mind, making you wonder how theyâre doing or what life would be like if youâd stayed in touch. In many cases, it doesnât mean you want to reconnectâit simply reflects how deeply those friendships became woven into your memories, leaving a lasting impression long after the friendship itself has ended.

Man was just sitting there generating moments like it was nothing. Every few seconds thereâs a new line that sounds like it shouldnât be funny but somehow sticks. The confidence in how he says everything is what really sells it. You can tell he wasnât even trying that hard either.

This fits into Personality-Driven Clip Humor, where the content relies entirely on the charisma and delivery of one individual rather than a structured setup and punchline. The format strings together multiple short, distinct moments that each feel quotable and repeatable. It works because the audience latches onto tone, voice, and subtle mannerisms instead of just the words themselves. Psychologically, it creates multiple entry points for engagement, allowing different viewers to attach to different moments. The repetition and unique phrasing make the clips easy to reuse and remix, increasing their longevity.

The video is from a livestream by Drake (2024) featuring Drake in a casual outdoor setting interacting with viewers, delivering lines like âWâs in the chat,â ânon-believers, underachievers, tweet-and-deleters,â and introducing âAnita Max Wynn.â The moment fits the caption because the stream unintentionally produced multiple distinct, repeatable lines and reactions in one session, turning a normal broadcast into a collection of viral moments.

Meet Leslie Shook, better known by her callsign âBitchinâ Bettyââthe voice behind many of the warning systems used in U.S. military aircraft. From âPull Up!â and âAltitude!â to âMissile Launch!â, âWarning!â, and countless other critical alerts, her recordings have guided pilots through high-workload and emergency situations for decades.

These voice warning systems are designed to deliver clear, unmistakable commands the instant a dangerous condition is detected. Rather than forcing pilots to interpret instrument readings during stressful moments, the aircraft provides immediate spoken alerts, helping crews react faster and maintain situational awareness. Itâs a perfect example of how human factors engineering enhances flight safety.

Although pilots may never meet the voice they hear in the cockpit, it has become one of the most recognizable sounds in military aviationâtrusted by generations of aviators around the world.

Phagocytes play a key role in stopping bacterial infections before they spread. Through a process called phagocytosis, these immune cells recognize and engulf invading bacteria, trapping them inside a compartment called a phagosome. This then fuses with a lysosome to form a phagolysosome, where enzymes, reactive oxygen species, and acidic conditions break the bacteria down.

By destroying bacteria at this early stage, phagocytes prevent them from dividing and multiplying, helping the body control infection before it can spread further.

Criselda Vasquezâs 2017 oil painting, The New American Gothic, powerfully reimagines Grant Woodâs classic 1930 masterpiece to honor modern Mexican immigrant labor. In this 72 by 48 inch artwork, the artist replaces the iconic Midwestern farmers with a stoic portrait of her own immigrant parents standing before a red work van. Instead of holding a pitchfork, her father grips a garden hoe, while her mother holds a plastic cleaning bucket filled with supplies. 

Through this strategic subversion, Vasquez challenges traditional notions of American identity and highlights the essential, often invisible workforce that sustains the country. The painting gained profound real-world resonance and widespread attention when it was revealed that the artistâs father, the very man depicted in the artwork, was later detained by immigration authorities and faced deportation.

On a quiet patch of open ground, two animals shared the same space but not the same understanding of what was happening.

A young goat stood with its head low and shoulders tense. Its legs shifted in small adjustments. It was practicing a charge. This is normal goat behavior. Goats test strength through forward bursts, head positioning, and timing. It helps them build coordination, balance, and dominance awareness. The motion looks simple, but it carries clear intent in animal language. It signals impact, pressure, and direction.

Nearby, a cat sat calmly watching.

The cat did not read force. It did not interpret competition. It focused on movement patterns, body rhythm, and proximity. Cats build understanding through repetition and association. Many of their social behaviors come from contact, grooming, and controlled interaction. They often translate unfamiliar actions into familiar categories, especially when no threat is detected.

The goat stepped back.

Its hooves scraped the ground lightly. Muscles tightened. Head lowered again. Then it moved forward in a short, controlled burst. Not fully aggressive. Not random. It was practice. A rehearsal of impact without full force.

The cat reacted differently from what the goat intended.

Instead of retreating, the cat leaned forward slightly. Its posture softened. Its tail relaxed. It interpreted the forward motion as engagement rather than confrontation. In its behavioral framework, approaching behavior from another animal often signals curiosity or social interaction rather than aggression.

The goat repeated the motion.

Another small charge forward. Controlled. Predictable. Consistent.

The cat responded by moving closer.

It rubbed its body against the air near the goat's path, lowering its head in a relaxed angle. It treated the movement as a greeting pattern. In feline behavior, approaching without tension often connects to social bonding signals like head bumps, scent exchange, and proximity acceptance.

Kangaroos are strong swimmers, and when pursued by dogs, they may move into water where they can use their forelimbs to hold or push a dog underwater as a defensive response. While this behavior has been documented, it is relatively uncommon and usually occurs when the kangaroo feels threatened.

Because dogs can trigger a kangaroo's fight-or-flight instincts, wildlife experts recommend keeping dogs leashed in areas where kangaroos are present and avoiding close encounters altogether. The safest outcome is for both the animal and the dog to be separated without escalating the situation.

In 1946, Kurt Chew-Een Lee made history as the first Chinese-American officer in the U.S. Marine Corps, entering a military where racial prejudice was still deeply entrenched.

Born in California to immigrant parents, Lee grew up determined to prove that Asian Americans were just as loyal, capable, and courageous as anyone else. When the Korean War erupted in 1950, he saw an opportunity to do exactly that.

Lee quickly gained a reputation for fearless leadership.
During a nighttime battle, he used an unconventional tactic that became legendary-shouting commands in Mandarin as he advanced toward enemy positions. The confusion it created among Chinese forces caused hesitation in their ranks, giving his Marines the opening they needed to push forward.

His extraordinary bravery earned him the Navy Cross, one of the nationâs highest military honors.

But Leeâs courage didnât stop there. During the brutal Chosin Reservoir campaign, despite being wounded, he launched a daring solo reconnaissance mission up a mountainside to locate enemy positions. The intelligence he gathered helped guide his battalion through encirclement and saved countless lives.

Kurt Chew-Een Lee didnât just fight Americaâs enemiesâ he fought the stereotypes and discrimination of his era.
Today, he is remembered as a war hero, a trailblazer, and a powerful symbol of resilience, leadership, and patriotism.

Reddit is a social media platform and online community where users can share content, participate in discussions, and vote on posts. Launched in 2005, it is organized into thousands of âsubreddits,â each focused on a specific topic, interest, or theme, ranging from news and science to hobbies, memes, and niche communities. Users can post text, links, images, or videos, and other users can upvote or downvote these submissions, which helps determine how visible the content becomes on the site. Reddit also allows for threaded comments, so discussions can be detailed, layered, and interactive.

What sets Reddit apart is its mix of anonymity and community-driven moderation. Users often interact using usernames rather than real names, which encourages open discussion but can also lead to controversial or unfiltered content. Subreddit moderators, who are volunteers, enforce rules specific to their communities to maintain order and relevance. Reddit has become influential in shaping online trends, hosting AMAs (âAsk Me Anythingâ sessions with celebrities or experts), and providing a space for people to find support, share ideas, and explore niche interests from around the world.

That purple glow is display tech that basically went extinct. ð ð

These are Japanese car head units from the late 90s and early 2000s, the era most audio enthusiasts still call the golden age. The glowing hero here is a Kenwood DPX-770MD, and the reason its display looks like liquid neon is that it does not use a backlit LCD like a modern screen.

It uses a self-emitting display where the pixels generate their own light, the same family of technology as vacuum fluorescent tubes. Nothing shines a light through it. The display itself is the light source.

This was the period when brands like Kenwood, Pioneer and Alpine were in an all-out engineering war. Motorized flip-out faceplates. Onboard digital signal processors. MiniDisc slots. Animated spectrum analyzers that danced to your music in colors LCDs of the time could not reproduce. Owning one was a status symbol on four wheels.

Then touchscreens arrived, LCDs got cheap, and that deep self-lit glow disappeared from dashboards almost overnight.

An entire era of dashboard engineering, lit by a technology we quietly left behind.

Interesting Fact:

The "Cuckooâs Egg" of Data Drift -

In MLOps, a model can be mathematically perfect but fail because of Data Drift. 

This happens when the "real world" changes but the modelâs environment doesn't.
 
In 2020, many high-frequency trading and inventory models broke because they couldn't process the sudden shift in human behavior during lockdowns.

MLOps teams now use Kullback-Leibler (KL) Divergence, a formula to measure how much the current data "distribution" has moved away from the training data to trigger an automatic "emergency" retraining.

The Last Emperor (1987) is an epic historical biographical drama directed by Bernardo Bertolucci that chronicles the remarkable life of Puyi, the last emperor of China's Qing dynasty. Beginning with his imprisonment in 1950, the film unfolds through a series of flashbacks that reveal how Puyi was crowned emperor as a young child and spent his early years confined within the majestic walls of the Forbidden City. Surrounded by luxury yet isolated from the outside world, he grows up struggling to understand the responsibilities and limitations of his extraordinary position.
As China undergoes sweeping political and social transformation, Puyi's imperial authority fades with the collapse of the Qing dynasty. Forced to adapt to a rapidly changing world, he experiences exile, manipulation by powerful political forces, and the loss of the identity he once believed defined him. His journey becomes one of self-discovery as he confronts the consequences of his past while searching for purpose in a society that has moved beyond monarchy.
Featuring a powerful performance by John Lone as Puyi, alongside Joan Chen, Peter O'Toole, and Vivian Wu, The Last Emperor is celebrated for its breathtaking cinematography, lavish production design, and emotionally rich storytelling. As the first Western film granted permission to shoot inside Beijing's Forbidden City, it offers an unparalleled sense of authenticity and grandeur. Winner of nine Academy Awards, including Best Picture and Best Director, the film remains a landmark historical epic admired for its visual beauty, historical scope, and deeply human exploration of power, identity, and redemption.

In the Arctic, the freezing climate naturally preserved food, allowing Indigenous communities to enjoy fresh and frozen fish as a vital part of their traditional way of life for generations. Nanook of the North (1922) introduced the world to Inuit life in the Canadian Arctic. The Inuit are Indigenous peoples who have lived across the Arctic regions of Canada, Greenland, Alaska, and Siberia for thousands of years. Their traditional way of life was built around hunting marine mammals, fishing, and adapting to extreme Arctic conditions.  The movie introduced millions of people to traditional Inuit life, including hunting, fishing, igloo building, and family life in the Arctic.  It is considered one of the worldâs first feature-length documentaries.

The Marriage License (1955) by Norman Rockwell #art #painting #artwork #arthistory

Norman Rockwell had asked an engaged couple to pose as the lovebirds in this painting, while Jason Braman, a retired town clerk, posed as the city official.

The painting was rather therapeutic for the widower, as it gave him something other than his grief to focus on.

Once the cover for the Saturday Evening Post came out, Bramanâs neighbors and friends recognized him. He would even offer to sign the covers, which he found amusing.

Something else that I noticed (and this is more of a pet theory than anything else) is that the man is covering his fiancÃ©eâs stomach with his hat. Is she pregnant? Is that why they seem to be in such a rush to get married?

There is a quiet harmony in bringing mid-century psychology out into the open air. 
This is a gentle nod to B.F. Skinner, the psychologist who proved actions can be guided by simple, positive rewards. Reimagined on a sunlit sidewalk with wild pigeons as the musicians, his theory becomes a soft, poetic spectacle.

Guided by the promise of food, the birds step onto the keys to create an ambient rhythm. 
It forms a beautiful loop: as the pigeons find their melody, the busy world is softly conditioned to slow down, leave the city noise behind, and share a moment of unexpected peace.

For one precious hour, Sam Goddard breaks free from his internal prison and can talk again. It's a fleeting moment of joy for him, his family and fiancee.

#OnThisDay in 2011 Australian Story filmed this incredible moment when a drug helped Sam find his voice. 

Sam was in his early 20s and playing soccer when he suffered the first of several catastrophic strokes that upended his life.

"The doctors continuously told us that he'd be brain damaged and said he'd never walk, he'd never breathe on his own, and I challenged it every step of the way," then-fiancee Sally told Australian Story.

Sam passed away in January 2018, age 31.

We're sharing archive clips like this to mark 30 years of #AustralianStory in 2026. Watch the episode in full via link in our bio.

This clip is from Reunited, the Dutch RTL4 show hosted by Yolanthe Cabau, and this episode aired on March 1, 2017. The story was about 32-year-old Ryan finally reuniting with his younger brother after 26 years. ï¿¼

Some videos do not need a big speech behind them. This is one of them.

Ryan had not seen his younger brother in 26 years, and when you know the backstory, the reunion hits even harder. After a 1990 car crash took their mother and younger brother, the two surviving brothers were separated. Ryan went to family in the Netherlands, while his brother stayed on Aruba with his stepfather. For more than two decades, they were still each otherâs only real piece of immediate family. ï¿¼

That is why this moment lands the way it does. It is not just two brothers hugging after a long time. It is two people finding their way back to the last living part of their old life. After everything they lost, that embrace feels bigger than a reunion. It feels like getting a piece of home back. ï¿¼

Context: RTL4âs Reunited, Ryan and his brother Rachid, reunion on Aruba / Dutch Caribbean ï¿¼
Year: 2017 ï¿¼

This video was only possible because of our friends over at Kim Eung Hwa and Korean Dance Acadmey @kimeunghwakoreandance , a non-profit in Koreatown LA that focuses on preserving and sharing the art of Korean traditional dance and music.  They were one of the first to be established in Ktown in 1980 and only a handful of these non-profits are still around.

They welcome people of all ages (4+ years), gender, and ethnicity who wish to learn about the richness of Korean culture.

This fall, the Kim Eung Hwa and Korean Dance Academy will premiere an original dance-drama marking the 100th anniversaries of both the June 10th Independence Movement and Arirang. The production will share the inspiring story of filmmaker and independence activist Na Woon-gyu, whose groundbreaking film Arirang became a symbol of hope, resilience, and Korean identity during one of the most challenging periods in Korea's history.

To learn more you can check out their website.

Over 12 NBA seasons with four teams â including the Grizzlies and the Heat â he averaged 10.5 points and 5.9 assists per game across 788 regular-season games. His crowning achievement came in 2006, when he served as the starting point guard for the Miami Heat's NBA Championship-winning squad. Though his career stats were solid, it was his behind-the-back passes, elbow passes, and improvisational flair that cemented his cult legend status in NBA history.

:::writing{variant="standard" id="48271"} Daycare was supposed to be another normal day of chaos, toys, barking, zoomies, and nonstop excitement. The little dog burst through the doors with the kind of energy only dogs can produce. His tail moved like a tiny motor. His paws barely touched the ground as he sprinted across the play area, greeting every dog like they were lifelong friends. Every corner of the daycare felt like an adventure waiting to happen.

The room echoed with happy barking and the sound of paws sliding across the floor. Tennis balls bounced in every direction. Plush toys were scattered everywhere. The little dog threw himself into the middle of it all without hesitation. One second he was chasing another puppy in circles, the next he was rolling onto his back demanding belly rubs from the daycare staff. His entire world was pure excitement.

He leaped onto soft mats, wrestled gently with bigger dogs, and proudly carried toys twice the size of his head. Every few minutes he would stop just long enough to catch his breath before launching himself back into the action. His ears bounced with every step. His tongue hung out in pure happiness. To anyone watching, he looked like the definition of joy.

The daycare workers laughed as they watched him race around the room like he owned the place. He had no worries. No fears. No stress. Just endless fun and endless energy. Dogs like him have a special way of turning ordinary moments into something unforgettable. They live completely in the present. Every game feels important. Every new friend feels exciting. Every moment feels worth celebrating.

But then everything changed in an instant.

In the middle of all the excitement, the little dog suddenly froze. His ears perked up sharply. His eyes locked onto the large front window. The energy in his body shifted immediately. Behind the glass stood the one person who mattered most in his world.

Dad.

The second he recognized him, the playful chaos disappeared from his mind completely.

Far East Movement were the first Asian American group to ever reach number 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and most people who listened to their music had no idea they were making history.

They came out of the underground scene in Los Angeles â years of performing at local clubs, giving away free music, and building a fanbase from nothing before any label paid attention. Then Like a G6 went to number 1 in 2010 and everything changed overnight. Rocketeer came right behind it and showed a completely different side of them. The song was emotional, melodic, and had a hook sung by Ryan Tedder â the lead singer of OneRepublic and one of the most prolific songwriters of the 2010s. Most people who loved Rocketeer never knew that was his voice on it.

The song hit number 7 on Billboard and proved they werenât just a party music act. But after the initial wave the mainstream moved on and one of the most groundbreaking groups in pop history faded into the background without the recognition they earned.

First Asian American group to ever top the Hot 100 and most people canât even name them.

Work has been a defining part of human life for thousands of years. From ancient farmers cultivating crops along river valleys to modern workers managing complex technologies, every society has depended on people contributing their skills, labor, and knowledge. Throughout history, work has built cities, connected nations through trade, advanced science, and driven innovation. While the tools and industries have changed dramatically, the fundamental idea remains the same: people working together to create, maintain, and improve the world around them.

For many people, work represents more than just earning a paycheck. It can provide structure, purpose, social connections, and opportunities for personal growth. At the same time, it often comes with challenges, deadlines, long hours, and responsibilities that test patience and resilience. Whether someone works in construction, healthcare, retail, education, technology, or any other field, their efforts contribute to a larger system that keeps society functioning. Though work is rarely glamorous every day, it remains one of the most important ways individuals shape both their own lives and the communities around them.

Before silicon chips existed, NASA relied on magnetic core memory to run the Apollo Program.

These computers used hand-woven grids of tiny magnetic rings, called cores. Each ring stored a single bit of data by flipping its magnetic direction, and once set, it held that information with zero power.

This made core memory incredibly durable and reliableâperfect for spaceflight. Itâs also where the term âcore dumpâ comes from, originally referring to reading out the physical memory cores.

Modern computing may be microscopic and digital, but its foundation was once tangible, manual, and built entirely on physics.

label_values.value:
It's interesting how subjective music can be, with one person's anthem being another's auditory discomfort. In the vast landscape of contemporary artists, certain sounds tend to stand out not for their harmonious quality or intricate lyrical depth, but for an altogether different impact on the listener. When considering the recent releases and discography of artists like KSI, there's a particular sonic signature that, for many, transcends the realm of simple preference and veers directly into what could be described as an unwelcome sonic intrusion. The aggressive vocal delivery, often basic rhythmic structures, and a production style that frequently prioritizes sheer volume over nuanced composition combine to create an experience that can feel less like entertainment and more like an aural assault. This isn't about personal taste in genre, but a broader observation about the inherent qualities of the sound being produced and its overall effect on the immediate environment, moving beyond mere background music to something far more pronounced and, at times, grating.

The argument that some musical outputs contribute to noise pollution isn't new, but it gains particular traction when the elements within a track actively work against principles of sound design that typically aim for a more pleasant or engaging listening experience. With KSI's tracks, the pervasive sense of a relentless, often uninspired, wall of sound can overwhelm rather than captivate. It often feels as though the emphasis is placed heavily on generating hype through loudness and repetition, rather than crafting compositions that offer genuine musicality or thoughtful progression. This approach can lead to a listening situation where the primary reaction isn't enjoyment or engagement, but a desire for the sound to cease, making it difficult to differentiate from other forms of unwanted, intrusive noise that disrupt peace and quiet. Ultimately, while artistic expression is diverse, the line between music and auditory annoyance can become blurred, transforming intended entertainment into an unintended source of sonic disruption for many.

label_values.label: Caption
label_values.value:
One of the hardest parts about being a caregiver is feeling like your heart is constantly being pulled in two directions.

I love including Max. I love watching him light up when he feels seen, loved, and part of the world around him. A lot of my life has been built around making sure he feels safe, included, and celebrated.

But that does not mean it is always easy.

Sometimes leaving without him feels heavy. Sometimes doing something for myself makes me feel guilty before I even get there. Sometimes I hate disappointing him, even when I know I am not doing anything wrong.

When you love someone like this, you want to bring them everywhere. You want to protect them from sadness, loneliness, and feeling left out. And when you cannot do that perfectly, it hurts.

I try to include Max as much as I can. He is my brother, my best friend, and one of the biggest blessings in my life.

But I am also learning that caregivers need care too.

We need time to breathe. Time to rest. Time to have our own experiences, our own friendships, our own quiet moments, and our own lives.

Taking time for yourself does not mean you are abandoning the person you love. It does not mean you are selfish. It means you are trying to stay whole enough to keep loving them well.

A lot of caregivers carry silent guilt. But guilt is not always proof that you did something wrong. Sometimes it is just proof that you care deeply.

So to anyone who takes care of someone they love: you are allowed to rest. You are allowed to have a life too. You are allowed to step away for a little while and still be a good caregiver.

I am still learning this.

Loving Max is one of the greatest honors of my life. And part of loving him well is making sure I do not lose myself in the process.

Caregivers deserve care too.

The Real-Life Legend Behind Nacho Libre

The cult comedy Nacho Libre wasnât just a wild invention â it was inspired by a real man with an unbelievable double life.

The film draws from the true story of Sergio Gutierrez Benitez, a Catholic priest who spent his days serving the church and his nights wrestling under the masked persona Fray Tormenta. For 23 years, he stepped into the ring not for fame, but to secretly raise money for the orphanage he ran, funding food, shelter, and education for children in need.

Though long retired from wrestling, Fray Tormentaâs mission never stopped. Now in his 80s, he continues supporting the orphanage that started it all. His legacy even inspired one of the children he cared for in the late â90s to take up the mask and carry on the tradition as Fray Tormenta Jr.

Itâs a real-life story so heartfelt and strange that Hollywood barely had to exaggerate it â proving that sometimes the wildest movie plots come straight from reality.

What if I told you thereâs a creature on Earth that is technically immortal?

Fun fact: The jellyfish species Turritopsis dohrnii, often called the immortal jellyfish, can reverse its own aging process. When injured, stressed, or near death, it performs a biological reset by transforming its adult cells back into their earliest form, essentially starting its life cycle over again. This process, known as transdifferentiation, is something no other animal has been observed doing naturally.

In theory, this jellyfish could repeat the cycle indefinitely, making it biologically immortal - not because it canât die, but because it doesnât age. Predators and disease can kill it, but time cannot. Scientists are studying this tiny creature in hopes of understanding cellular regeneration, aging, and even potential medical breakthroughs for humans.

This remarkable species challenges everything we think we know about life and longevity. It proves that nature still holds secrets far stranger - and far more advance- than science fiction. The smallest organisms often hide the biggest mysteries.
